text:
A: Hiya, can you hear me okay?
B: Yeah, I can hear you, love. Hiya, I'm Nicola.
A: I'm Megan. Sorry, I always say that at the start, like the internet's going to go.
B: Ah, you're fine. How are you doing? Have they worn you out yet?
A: A bit, yeah. I'm okay, though. Erm, I'm in Stockton, Norton really. Where are you?
B: St Helens, up by Liverpool. I'll be honest, when I saw your photo I thought, she looks like me when I was starting out in care. Tired but capable.
A: Oh, that's really nice. I'm not in care, but sort of near it. I'm doing radiography, second year, so X-rays. And I thought you looked really easy to talk to. You reminded me a bit of my nanna, actually.
B: Your nanna! Oh, I'll take that, love, even if it makes me feel ancient.
A: Sorry, I meant it in a nice way! She's lovely. I do jigsaws with her most Sundays.
B: No, I know you did, I'm only teasing. Radiography, though. I've had more X-rays than hot dinners, me. I've got rheumatoid arthritis, so it's hands, feet, chest, the lot.
A: Oh no. Do you find it alright, having them done?
B: Mostly, yeah. The ones I remember are the radiographers who don't rush you. When your hands are bad and someone's trying to get your fingers flat on the plate, and they just say, take your time, there's no hurry. That makes the whole day better, do you know what I mean?
A: Yeah. That's kind of what I worry about, getting it wrong with someone like that. I'm good with older patients, I think, but I check everything about five times.
B: Better that than not checking. I did care work for years, and the ones who worried were always the good ones.
A: That's sort of what my supervisor says. Did you like care work?
B: I loved it. Sitting with people, listening. I'm off sick now, about four years. I miss it.
A: I bet. Erm, sorry, I'm just thinking what to ask. What do you do in the day, then?
B: Read, mostly. Watch the birds. I do little watercolours when my hands let me. And telly, I watch these Danish crime dramas with subtitles.
A: I couldn't do subtitles, I'd be on my phone and miss it. I'm Bake Off and Gogglebox. And Friends repeats, honestly.
B: Oh, Bake Off's lovely. My Ellie's mad on cooking now, she's fifteen. TikTok recipes.
A: My brother's sixteen and he just eats. My mam made mince and dumplings for tea and he'd had half of it before I got in.
B: Mince and dumplings! We call it tea up here too. My treat's a chip barm.
A: Mine's a parmo on a Friday. I share it with my brother though, I can't finish a whole one.
B: What's a parmo, love?
A: Oh, it's a Teesside thing. Breaded chicken with béchamel sauce and cheese on top, with chips. It's massive.
B: Oh, that sounds dangerous. I'd have a go at that.
A: You should, if you're ever up. Is that time already?
B: I think so. It's been lovely, Megan. Give your nanna my best.
A: I will. Thank you, it was really nice talking to you.
